text: starting raw count matrix, SCPreProcess automatically perform Seurat preprocess (including NormalizeData, FindVariableFeatures, ScaleData, RunPCA, FindNeighbors, FindClusters, RunTSNE, RunUMAP). SCPreProcess returns fully preprocessed Seurat object downstream use. Build initial Seurat object Imports count matrix. Applies first, coarse filters: genes must detected >= min_cells cells; cells must contain >= min_features genes. Attaches optional sample metadata. Mitochondrial QC (default: ) single regular expression (^MT- ^mt-) used compute percentage mitochondrial reads per cell. metric stored object$percent.mt later filtering. Cell filtering (default: ) Cells retained satisfy following: nFeature_RNA lies lower upper bounds defined data_filter.nFeature_RNA_thresh. percent.mt user-defined cut-(data_filter.percent.mt). Normalisation, variable-feature selection scaling Encapsulated ProcessSeuratObject(): Counts normalised chosen method (default: LogNormalize). Highly variable features identified using requested algorithm (default: vst). Expression values features scaled unit variance. Append extra observations input object contains obs slot, merged object@meta.data. Dimensionality reduction clusteringClusterAndReduce() runs: PCA -> nearest-neighbour graph -> Louvain clustering (resolution parameterised). UMAP two-dimensional visualization. Optionally removes small low-quality clusters. Tumour-cell flaggingFilterTumorCell() creates binary label (1 = Tumour, 0 = Normal) column specified column2only_tumor. new label can used downstream restrict analyses malignant cells.
code: your_seurat <- SCPreProcess(   your_matrix,   meta_data = NULL,   project = "Screen_Single_Cell", # Parameters used in Seurat preprocessing pipeline   min_cells = 400,   min_features = 0,   normalization_method = "LogNormalize",   scale_factor = 10000,   selection_method = "vst",   resolution = 0.6,   dims = 1:10,   verbose = TRUE,   future_global_maxsize = 6 * 1024^3,   quality_control = TRUE,   quality_control.pattern = c("^MT-"), # human for '^MT-', mouse for '^mt-', or specify your own pattern   data_filter = TRUE,   data_filter.nFeature_RNA_thresh = c(200, 6000), # [min, max]   data_filter.percent.mt = 20,   column2only_tumor = NULL,   ... )

title: Full Tutorial
text: BulkPreProcess performs comprehensive quality control bulk RNA-seq data. Key parameters BulkPreProcess: data: Expression matrix genes rows samples columns, list containing count_matrix sample_info. sample_info: Sample information data frame (optional), ignored data list. gene_symbol_conversion: Whether convert Ensembl version IDs TCGA version IDs genes SymbolConvert Section 2.2.2, default TRUE. check: Whether perform detailed quality checks, default TRUE. min_count_threshold: Minimum count threshold gene filtering, default 10. min_gene_expressed: Minimum number samples gene must expressed , default 3. min_total_reads: Minimum total reads per sample, default 1e6. min_genes_detected: Minimum number genes detected per sample, default 10000. min_correlation: Minimum correlation threshold samples, default 0.8. n_top_genes: Number top variable genes PCA analysis, default 500. show_plot_results: Whether generate PCA visualization plots, default TRUE. verbose: Whether output detailed information, default TRUE. Suppose bulk RNA-seq count data sample information, want perform comprehensive preprocessing quality control. can refer use following code: function returns filtered count matrix applying quality control steps. order filtering : first genes, samples.
code: # Example usage of BulkPreProcess filtered_counts <- BulkPreProcess(    data = your_count_matrix,    sample_info = your_sample_info,    gene_symbol_conversion = TRUE,    check = TRUE,    min_count_threshold = 10,    min_samples_expressed = 3,    min_total_reads = 1e6,    min_genes_detected = 10000,    min_correlation = 0.8,    n_top_genes = 500,    show_plot_results = TRUE,    verbose = TRUE )

Initialize output     na_info <- list()      cli::cli_h1("NA Value Check (data.table optimized)")     cli::cli_alert_info("Checking object with dimensions: {.val {dim(data)}}")      # Handle 1D data (vectors)     if (!is_2d) {         na_count <- sum(is.na(data))         na_positions <- which(is.na(data))         na_info$positions <- na_positions         na_info$count <- na_count          if (na_count == 0) {             cli::cli_alert_success("No NA values found in the vector!")         }          cli::cli_alert_warning("Found {.val {na_count}} NA value{?s} in vector")          if (length(na_positions) > 0 && max_print > 0) {             positions_to_show <- na_positions[                 1:min(max_print, length(na_positions))             ]             cli::cli_text("Positions: {.val {positions_to_show}}")              if (length(na_positions) > max_print) {                 cli::cli_text(                     "{.val {length(na_positions) - max_print}} additional positions not shown"                 )             }         }          # For named vectors         if (!is.null(names(data))) {             na_names <- names(data)[na_positions]             na_info$names <- na_names              if (length(na_names) > 0 && max_print > 0) {                 names_to_show <- na_names[1:min(max_print, length(na_names))]                 cli::cli_text("Names: {.val {names_to_show}}")             }         }     } else {         # Handle 2D data (dataframes, matrices, data.tables)         # Use data.table for efficient NA counting         na_count <- dt[, sum(is.na(.SD))]         na_info$count <- na_count          if (na_count == 0) {             cli::cli_alert_success("No NA values found in the 2D data!")         }          cli::cli_alert_warning(             "Found {.val {na_count}} NA value{?s} in 2D data"         )          # Get NA positions efficiently without melt warning         if (max_print > 0) {             # Create a matrix of logical values indicating NA positions             na_matrix <- is.na(as.matrix(dt))             na_positions <- which(na_matrix, arr.ind = TRUE)              # Convert to data.table and add column names             na_positions_dt <- data.table::as.data.table(na_positions)             colnames(na_positions_dt) <- c("row", "col")             na_positions_dt$col_name <- colnames(dt)[na_positions_dt$col]              na_info$positions <- na_positions_dt              if (nrow(na_positions_dt) > 0) {                 positions_to_show <- na_positions_dt[                     1:min(max_print, nrow(na_positions_dt)),                 ]                  cli::cli_text(                     "First {.val {nrow(positions_to_show)}} position{?s}:"                 )                  for (i in 1:nrow(positions_to_show)) {                     cli::cli_text(                         "  Row {.val {positions_to_show$row[i]}}, Col {.val {positions_to_show$col_name[i]}} (index: {.val {positions_to_show$col[i]}})"                     )                 }                  if (na_count > max_print) {                     cli::cli_text(                         "{.val {na_count - max_print}} additional positions not shown"                     )                 }             }         }          # Column-wise summary using data.table         col_na <- dt[, lapply(.SD, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))]         col_na <- unlist(col_na)         col_na <- col_na[col_na > 0]          if (length(col_na) > 0) {             na_info$column_na <- col_na              cli::cli_text("Column-wise NA counts:")             for (col in names(col_na)) {                 cli::cli_text("  {.field {col}}: {.val {col_na[col]}}")             }         }     }      return(invisible(na_info)) }
